title.en: C’était: looking back at a situation

summary.en: Recognise a familiar identifying pattern in the past.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 6.

Episode 6 describes a project with *c'était mon idée*. The familiar *c'est* pattern has moved into the past: *était* is an imperfect form of *être*.

The imperfect often presents a past situation, description or background. It need not describe a completed event with a clear endpoint. The speaker's point here is whose idea the project was, rather than a sequence of actions performed on it.

`c'` is the shortened form of *ce* before the verb. Learn *c'était* as a recognisable spoken unit, while still noticing the noun phrase that follows it.

When listening again, distinguish a background description from a newly completed action. French can express those jobs with different past-tense patterns. You do not need to translate every past form into the same English template to understand the scene.
